2027-05-16.title: First Sunday of the Apostles · The Feast of Pentecost
2027-05-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: A priestly kingdom and a holy nation
The Holy Spirit comes down on the apostles
Varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit
The Spirit of truth will guide you into all the truth
2027-05-16.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), the seven weeks that begin at Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari; from Pentecost “The Angel of the Lord” (the Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. Pentecost is a Feast of Our Lord, and the Season of the Apostles (Šleehe) begins today. The calendar gives longer forms: Exodus 19:1–9 with 20:13–21; Acts 2:1–21; 1 Corinthians 12:1–27; John 14:15–16, 25–26; 15:26–16:15. In the Latin calendar Pentecost Sunday closes the Easter season today. St Simon Stock (16 May) gives way to the feast (verify locally).
2027-05-16.verse: All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them ability.
theo: Fifty days ago we sang the Resurrection; today the fifty days reach their goal. “When the day of Pentecost had come, they were all together in one place.” Pentecost was already a great feast for the Jewish people, the Feast of Weeks, the harvest festival kept fifty days after Passover, and in later Jewish tradition it was also linked with the giving of the Law on Sinai. That is why our Church opens the feast with Exodus 19. “On the third new moon after the Israelites had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that very day, they came into the wilderness of Sinai.” God speaks to Moses from the mountain: “You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself.” Then the promise: “you shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation.” God comes in a dense cloud, and a few verses later the mountain is wrapped in smoke “because the LORD had descended upon it in fire” (Exodus 19:18). At Sinai, fire on the mountain gave Israel the Law on tablets of stone; in the upper room, fire on each head writes the new law of love on human hearts, as the prophet had promised: “I will put my spirit within you” (Ezekiel 36:27). The people at Sinai answered, “Everything that the LORD has spoken we will do”; at Pentecost the Spirit gives the power to do it. Peter would later write to the baptised the very words of Sinai: “you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God’s own people” (1 Peter 2:9).

Luke describes the event with signs that every reader of the Scriptures would recognise. “Suddenly from heaven there came a sound like the rush of a violent wind, and it filled the entire house where they were sitting.” Wind and breath are one word in Hebrew and in our Syriac tradition: the breath God breathed into Adam (Genesis 2:7), the wind Ezekiel summoned over the dry bones, the breath of the Risen Lord who said, “Receive the Holy Spirit” (John 20:22). “Divided tongues, as of fire, appeared among them, and a tongue rested on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them ability.” The Spirit does not come as a general mood over a crowd; a tongue rests on each one. And the first thing the Spirit does is make them speak. The Church is born speaking, born on mission. The disciples who had hidden behind locked doors now go out into the street. Mary is among them; the Spirit who overshadowed her at Nazareth to form the body of Christ now comes down to form his Body, the Church.

The crowd that gathers is made of “devout Jews from every nation under heaven living in Jerusalem”, and each one hears the apostles “speaking in the native language of each.” Then Luke lists the nations, and we Syro-Malabar Christians should listen closely: “Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and residents of Mesopotamia”. These are the lands of the East where the Gospel soon took root, the lands of the Church of the East, whose faith, liturgy and Syriac language came to the Thomas Christians of Malabar. At Pentecost our own spiritual ancestors were, in a sense, already standing in the crowd. At Babel human pride had confused the languages and scattered the peoples (Genesis 11:9); at Pentecost the Spirit does not abolish the languages but makes the one Gospel heard in each of them. That is why the Church can pray in Syriac and Malayalam, in Latin and Tamil, in English and Hindi, and still be one. The reaction is mixed: “All were amazed and perplexed, saying to one another, ‘What does this mean?’ But others sneered and said, ‘They are filled with new wine.’” The Spirit's work always provokes both wonder and mockery. Joel had promised, and Peter will soon proclaim, that God would pour out his Spirit on all flesh (Acts 2:16–17). It has happened.

Paul tells the Corinthians how to recognise the Spirit. Not by spectacle, but by a confession: “no one can say ‘Jesus is Lord’ except by the Holy Spirit.” Every time a child in our homes lisps the name of Jesus, every time a dying person whispers, Eeshoye, the Spirit is at work. Then Paul describes the Church as a body with many gifts: “Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of services, but the same Lord; and there are varieties of activities, but it is the same God who activates all of them in everyone.” Notice the Holy Trinity in those three lines: Spirit, Lord, God. The gifts differ: wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, prophecy, discernment, tongues. But the purpose is one: “To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.” No gift is for showing off, and no one is without a gift. The catechist who teaches on Sunday morning, the choir member, the parent who prays with the children, the youth who visits the sick, the elderly woman who prays the rosary for the parish: all of these “are activated by one and the same Spirit, who allots to each one individually just as the Spirit chooses.” We received the seal of this Spirit in our Thailabhishekam, the anointing with holy Myron given in our Church together with Baptism.

In the Gospel Jesus prepares his disciples for this day. They are sad that he is leaving, and he says something astonishing: “it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.” The Ascension was not a loss; it opened the way for the gift. The Spirit will “prove the world wrong about sin and righteousness and judgment”: he shows the world its sin of unbelief, reveals the righteousness of Christ who returns to the Father, and announces that “the ruler of this world has been condemned.” And for the disciples: “When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth”. He does not invent a new Gospel: “he will take what is mine and declare it to you. All that the Father has is mine.” Here, on the threshold of next Sunday's feast of the Holy Trinity, we glimpse the life of God: the Father who gives all to the Son, the Son who sends the Spirit, the Spirit who glorifies the Son. Today the Season of the Apostles begins, the seven weeks in which our Church contemplates how the Spirit sent the apostles to the ends of the earth, and how one of them, Mar Thoma, came to our shores. The Spirit who came down in the upper room is the same Spirit who keeps the faith alive in Kerala homes and parishes. Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.
conn: At Babel “the LORD confused the language of all the earth; and from there the LORD scattered them abroad” (Genesis 11:9); at Pentecost the scattered hear one Gospel in their own languages (Acts 2:6).
Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke “because the LORD had descended upon it in fire” (Exodus 19:18); at Pentecost tongues as of fire rest on each disciple (Acts 2:3).
God “breathed into his nostrils the breath of life” (Genesis 2:7); the Risen Lord “breathed on them and said to them, ‘Receive the Holy Spirit’” (John 20:22).
“So stay here in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high” (Luke 24:49); “you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you” (Acts 1:8).
Moses longed: “Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!” (Numbers 11:29); Joel promised it (Joel 2:28).

“The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD” (Isaiah 11:2); the Spirit who rested on Christ is given to his Body.
“God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us” (Romans 5:5).
altar: In every Holy Qurbana the priest calls down the Holy Spirit upon the bread and wine in the Epiclesis, and the Spirit who came at Pentecost makes them the Body and Blood of Christ. Pentecost happens again on our altar.
The same Spirit is asked to come upon us, that we who receive the one Body may become one body, each with our gift, for the common good.
outline: Fifty days, and the harvest feast of Israel.
Point 1 · A priestly kingdom and a holy nation
Sinai, the cloud, the fire and the law written on hearts.
Point 2 · A tongue rested on each
Wind, fire and the Church born speaking; Mary in the upper room.
Point 3 · Each heard in their own language
Parthians, Medes, Mesopotamia: our own ancestors in faith, and Babel undone.
Point 4 · Varieties of gifts, the same Spirit
Jesus is Lord, and gifts for the common good.
The Spirit of truth guiding the Church, and Mar Thoma landing on our shore.
live: Begin and end each day this week by saying slowly: Jesus is Lord, and ask the Spirit to make it true in you.
Ask yourself what gift the Spirit has given you, and offer it this month to your parish for the common good.
Speak the Gospel in another's language (Acts 2:6)
Explain your faith this week to someone in words they understand: a child, a colleague, a friend of another faith, with respect.
From today pray “The Angel of the Lord” at morning, noon and evening, as our Church does in the Season of the Apostles.
fathers: As dry flour cannot become one loaf without water, so we who are many could not become one in Christ without the water that comes from heaven. Our bodies received unity through the washing of baptism, and our souls through the Spirit, the dew of God poured out at Pentecost.

The rain that comes down from heaven is one and the same, yet it becomes white in the lily, red in the rose, purple in the violet. So the Holy Spirit, one and undivided, gives to each as he wills: to one wisdom, to another prophecy, to another the power to drive out demons, and the Spirit himself is not changed.
magis: On that day the Holy Trinity is fully revealed; the Kingdom announced by Christ is open to those who believe in him, and the Church is manifested to the world.

When the work the Father gave the Son was accomplished, the Holy Spirit was sent on the day of Pentecost to sanctify the Church continually; then the Church was openly displayed to the crowds and the spread of the Gospel began.

Only when the hour has arrived for his glorification does Jesus promise the coming of the Holy Spirit; the Spirit will be with the disciples for ever, teaching them and guiding them into all the truth.
What the soul is to the human body, the Holy Spirit is to the Body of Christ, which is the Church (St Augustine).

Charisms, extraordinary or simple and humble, are graces of the Holy Spirit that directly or indirectly benefit the Church; they are to be accepted with gratitude, and charity is the true measure of them.
saints: First Sunday of the Apostles, the Feast of Pentecost, a Feast of Our Lord; the Season of the Apostles begins. In the Latin calendar Pentecost Sunday, which closes the Easter season. St Simon Stock gives way to the feast.

17–23 May: first week of the Apostles. Mon 17: Mary, Mother of the Church (listed in the First Set without proper readings; in the Latin calendar an obligatory memorial). Thu 20: anniversary of the inauguration of the first Syro-Malabar Bishops' Synod (1993). Fri 21: the Friday of Gold, the first Friday of the Apostles. Sun 23: Second Sunday of the Apostles, the Feast of the Holy Trinity.
2027-05-16.prayer: Father, on this holy day you fulfilled the promise of your Son and sent the Holy Spirit upon the apostles gathered with Mary, the Mother of Jesus. Pour out the same Spirit on your Church spread throughout the world, on our Syro-Malabar Church, heir of Mar Thoma, and on our families. As at Sinai you made a holy nation, make us a priestly people who live by the law of love written on our hearts. Let the Spirit of truth guide us into all the truth, give each of us our gift for the common good, and loosen our tongues to proclaim in every language that Jesus is Lord. Glory to you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, now and for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Exodus: at Sinai God makes Israel a priestly kingdom and a holy nation, and comes down in cloud and fire.
Acts: wind and tongues of fire; the apostles filled with the Spirit speak, and each hears in his own language.
Paul: no one can say “Jesus is Lord” except by the Holy Spirit; many gifts, one Spirit, for the common good.
Jesus: it is to your advantage that I go; the Spirit of truth will guide you into all the truth.
2027-05-16.action: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” slowly before every task today, and begin praying the Angelus again.
2027-05-16.question: What gift has the Spirit given me, and am I using it for the common good?
catechism: Pentecost reveals the Trinity and manifests the Church.
The Spirit sanctifies the Church and sends her on mission.
kidsaint: Peter was a fisherman who once was so afraid that he said he did not even know Jesus. But on the day of Pentecost the Holy Spirit came like wind and fire, and Peter stood up in front of thousands of people and told them bravely that Jesus is risen! That day about three thousand people were baptised. Lesson: the Holy Spirit makes us brave to talk about Jesus!
2027-05-16.special: First Sunday of the Apostles: the Feast of Pentecost. The Season of the Apostles begins.
term: The Syriac name of the Holy Spirit, used in our liturgy (Malayalam റൂഹാദ്കുദ്ശാ). Ruha means spirit, wind and breath, like the Hebrew ruach; Qudsha means holiness. The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Holy Trinity, “the Lord, the Giver of life, who proceeds from the Father” and is worshipped and glorified with the Father and the Son.

family.explain: After Jesus went up to heaven, his friends and Mother Mary waited and prayed in a room in Jerusalem. On the day of Pentecost they heard a sound like a strong wind, and little flames like fire came and rested on each one of them. They were filled with the Holy Spirit! Then they went out and told everyone about Jesus, and people from many countries understood them in their own language. The Holy Spirit came to us too, when we were baptised.
family.intention: We pray for the whole Church, that the Holy Spirit may make us brave and loving, and for people who do not yet know Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing can each of us do this week with the gift the Holy Spirit has given us?”

illus: A Syro-Malabar family from Thrissur moved to a city in the Gulf, and on their first Pentecost there they went to the big parish church. In one courtyard they heard prayers in Malayalam and Tamil, Konkani and Tagalog, Arabic and English; in the church a Holy Qurbana was being celebrated in Malayalam while another Mass was ending in another language. Their ten-year-old daughter, a little lost, asked her father, “Appa, how can it all be one Church if everyone is saying different things?” He thought for a moment and said, “Listen to the end of each prayer.” She stood near the door, and from each group she heard the same Name, said in every accent. That evening she wrote in her school diary: “Today I heard Jesus in eight languages. Pentecost is still happening.”

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love. As you came upon the apostles gathered with Mary, come upon us now. Amen. Alleluia!
share: You shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation (Exodus 19:6). How do I live as one consecrated to God?
All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:4). Where do I need the Spirit's fire in my life?
To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good (1 Corinthians 12:7). What is my gift, and how can I serve with it?
He will guide you into all the truth (John 16:13). In what decision do I need the guidance of the Spirit?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, renew the face of the earth.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that the Spirit may renew her in holiness, unity and courage for mission.
For our Syro-Malabar Church at the start of the Season of the Apostles, that she may be faithful to the apostolic faith of Mar Thoma.
For all Christians, that the Spirit may lead us to the unity Christ prayed for.
For those who do not yet know Christ, that they may hear the Gospel in their own language and heart.
For the young people of our parish, that they may discover and use the gifts of the Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you sent the Spirit of your Son upon the apostles gathered with Mary. Send him upon us, make us one, distribute your gifts among us, and send us out to proclaim that Jesus is Lord. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, today is Pentecost, the fiftieth day, the Feast of Our Lord that crowns the Season of the Resurrection and opens the Season of the Apostles. Pentecost was already a Jewish feast, the harvest festival, linked by tradition with the giving of the Law on Sinai. So our first reading takes us to Sinai, where God told Israel: “you shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation” (Exodus 19:6).

At Sinai God came in cloud and fire and gave his Law on stone. In the upper room he comes in wind and fire and writes his law of love on hearts. “All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit” (Acts 2:4). A tongue of fire rested on each one. Mary was there with them. The Spirit who formed Christ in her womb now forms his Body, the Church.

The first thing the Spirit does is make the apostles speak. Frightened men go out into the street. And people from many nations hear them each “in the native language of each” (Acts 2:6): Parthians, Medes, Elamites and residents of Mesopotamia. Those are the lands of the Church of the East, from which our own liturgy and our Syriac heritage came. Babel scattered the peoples; Pentecost gathers them into one Church with many tongues.

Paul says: “no one can say ‘Jesus is Lord’ except by the Holy Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:3). There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit, and each gift is given “for the common good” (12:7). No one in this church today is without a gift. We received the Spirit's seal in our Baptism and Thailabhishekam. The question is whether we use our gift for others.

Jesus told the sad disciples: “it is to your advantage that I go away” (John 16:7). He went to the Father so that the Advocate could come. “When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth” (16:13). The Spirit takes what belongs to Christ and gives it to us; and next Sunday we shall celebrate the Holy Trinity whom he reveals.

Today the Season of the Apostles begins. The Spirit who sent the apostles to the ends of the earth brought Mar Thoma to our shores. Let us not keep the fire to ourselves. Let us say every day, Come, Holy Spirit, and let us go out, each with our gift, to tell the world that Jesus is Lord. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, on Pentecost the Holy Spirit came like a strong wind and like little flames of fire on Jesus' friends and on Mother Mary. Then they were not afraid any more!
You received the Holy Spirit when you were baptised. Today, say this little prayer: “Come, Holy Spirit, make me brave and kind.”

opts.a: The Advocate who convicts and consoles
intro: Jesus calls the Holy Spirit the Advocate. He is the defender who stands beside us, and also the one who shows the world the truth about sin, righteousness and judgment.

points.h: It is to your advantage that I go
sub: The Spirit of wisdom and understanding.
points.apply: Pray each morning: Come, Holy Spirit, stand beside me today.

points.h: He will prove the world wrong about sin
sub: The Spirit shows us our sin.
Not to condemn, but to heal.
Receive the Holy Spirit; forgive sins.
points.apply: Make a good confession in this Season of the Apostles.

sub: A Spirit-filled life makes Christ known.
points.apply: Ask the Spirit to help you speak of Christ to one person this week.

concl: The Spirit stands beside us, convicts us of sin and glorifies Christ.
Pentecost is the gift of a Defender who never leaves us.
opts.resolve: In this Season of the Apostles I will make a good confession and pray daily for the Spirit's help.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the night before he died Jesus saw that his disciples were full of sorrow. He told them: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you (John 16:7). Today, at Pentecost, the Advocate has come.

The word Advocate means one who is called to stand beside you, a defender, a counsellor. Isaiah foretold that the spirit of the LORD would rest on the Messiah: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might (Isaiah 11:2). That same Spirit is now given to the Church and to each of us. We are never alone.

But Jesus also said: when he comes, he will prove the world wrong about sin and righteousness and judgment (John 16:8). The Spirit shows us our sin, not to crush us but to heal us. On Easter evening the risen Lord breathed on the apostles and said: receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them (John 20:22–23). Every confession is a little Pentecost. God promised through Ezekiel: a new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you (Ezekiel 36:26).

And Jesus said of the Spirit: he will glorify me, because he will take what is mine and declare it to you (John 16:14). The Spirit does not draw attention to himself. He makes Jesus known. Joel had promised: I will pour out my spirit on all flesh (Joel 2:28). Today that promise is kept, and every baptised person is called to make Christ known.

So let us pray each morning: Come, Holy Spirit, stand beside me today. Let us make a good confession in this Season of the Apostles. And let us ask the Spirit to give us the courage to speak of Christ, and to receive him with burning hearts at the Holy Qurbana. Alleluia! Amen.

opts.a: Mary in the upper room, and the Spirit at our altar
intro: Before Pentecost the disciples were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with Mary, the mother of Jesus. The Spirit came on a praying Church, and he still comes on every altar.

sub: How good when kindred live together.
The Spirit comes to a united Church.
points.apply: Make peace with someone in your parish or family before next Sunday.

sub: The Spirit came upon her at Nazareth.
Now she prays with the apostles.
points.apply: Pray the Rosary this week asking Mary to obtain the Spirit for your family.

sub: The Spirit is invoked in every Qurbana.
points.apply: At the next Qurbana, pay attention to the prayer calling down the Holy Spirit.

concl: The Spirit came upon a Church united in prayer with Mary.
He still descends at every Qurbana to make the gifts holy and to make us one.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray with Mary for the Spirit and make peace with someone before next Sunday.
homily: Dear friends, before the great day of Pentecost, the apostles did not organise a campaign. They prayed. Luke says: all these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14). And when the day came, they were all together in one place (Acts 2:1).

The Psalm says: how very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity (Psalm 133:1). The Spirit came upon a Church that was united and praying. If our families and parishes want the fire of the Spirit, we must first be together, forgiving one another and praying with one heart.

Mary was there. Long before the apostles, the Spirit had come upon her. At Nazareth the angel had said to her: the Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you (Luke 1:35). The Spirit who formed Christ in her womb now forms the Body of Christ, the Church. That is why we call her Mother of the Church. Where Mary prays, the Spirit is near.

At Mount Carmel, when Elijah prayed, the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the offering (1 Kings 18:38). Paul speaks of an offering made acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit (Romans 15:16). In every Holy Qurbana our Church calls upon the Holy Spirit to come down upon the bread and wine. The fire of Pentecost falls again on our altar, the gifts become the Body and Blood of Christ, and we who receive them are made one.

So in this Season of the Apostles let us make peace with someone before next Sunday. Let us pray the Rosary, asking Mary to obtain the Spirit for our families. And at the next Holy Qurbana, when the Spirit is invoked, let us bow our hearts and say: Come, Holy Spirit. Alleluia! Amen.

intro: Theme: “All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them ability.”
On the Feast of Pentecost: Sinai fulfilled, the Church born speaking, Babel undone, the gifts of the one Spirit, and the Spirit of truth who guides us into all the truth.

points.h: A priestly kingdom and a holy nation
q: but you shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation.
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God’s own people, in order that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises this week, and offer each day to God as a member of his holy people.

points.h: Each heard in their own language
q: Therefore it was called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of all the earth; and from there the LORD scattered them abroad over the face of all the earth.
And at this sound the crowd gathered and was bewildered, because each one heard them speaking in the native language of each.
points.apply: Pray for the unity of the Church in all her rites and languages, and speak of your faith to one person this week.

points.h: Varieties of gifts, the same Spirit
q: Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!
To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.
points.apply: Offer one gift of yours this month to the service of your parish.

points.h: The Spirit of truth will guide you
sub: It is to your advantage that I go.
All that the Father has is mine.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth;
points.apply: Before each decision this week, pray: Come, Holy Spirit, guide me into the truth.

concl: The Spirit who came down on the apostles gathered with Mary makes us a holy people, one Church in many tongues, and gives each of us a gift for others.
As the Season of the Apostles begins, let us receive the fire and carry it out, as Mar Thoma carried it to our land.
2027-05-16.resolve: This week, pray “Come, Holy Spirit” each morning, pray the Angelus, and use one gift of yours for the common good.
